hints.title: Single-Pass Three-Way Partitioning Obstacle
hints.text: A standard comparison sort takes logarithmic factor overhead and a two-pass counting approach reads the array twice. How can you partition items with three distinct values into sorted segments in a single pass using constant extra space?

hints.title: Dutch National Flag Invariant
hints.text: Divide the sequence into four regions: zeros at the start, ones in the middle, twos at the end, and unexamined elements between the middle and end boundaries.

hints.title: Three-Way Pointer Swap Procedure
hints.text: Maintain low, mid, and high pointers. While mid is less than or equal to high, inspect nums[mid]. If zero, swap nums[low] with nums[mid] and advance both low and mid. If one, simply increment mid. If two, swap nums[mid] with nums[high] and decrement high without advancing mid.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 300)
complexity.notes: Dutch National Flag 3-way partition in a single pass with O(1) memory.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: General comparison sorting runs in O(N log N) time and does not exploit the fixed 3-value domain constraint.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Counting sort requires two passes over the array; the Dutch National Flag partition sorts in-place in exactly one pass.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Knowing why mid does not advance when swapping with high (the swapped element from high has not yet been processed).
